Bayesian model-averaged benchmark dose

Source: R/bmdbayes.R
bmdbayes.Rd

The posterior distribution of the benchmark dose averaged over dose-response models fitted in the BMD parameterisation with priors, as in the Bayesian benchmark dose modelling of EFSA (2022): the models are weighted by their posterior probabilities, from their marginal likelihoods (marglik), and the BMD and its credible interval are the median and quantiles of the mixture of the posterior distributions of the BMD of the models.

Usage

bmdbayes(
  ...,
  prior.weights = NULL,
  method = c("laplace", "is"),
  n = 5000,
  df = 4
)

# S3 method for class 'bmdbayes'
coef(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'bmdbayes'
confint(object, parm = NULL, level = 0.9, ...)

bmdbayesmodels(object, level = 0.9)

# S3 method for class 'bmdbayes'
print(x, digits = max(3L, getOption("digits") - 3L), ...)

Arguments

...

drmTMB objects fitted in the BMD parameterisation (bmdpar of drmTMB) with the same benchmark response and definition, the same prior for the BMD (prior=list(bmd=...)) and proper priors for all estimated parameters, to the same doses, responses and weights; the models and families may differ. A single model is allowed. Models are labelled by their argument names (e.g. LL = fit1) or, if unnamed, by the expressions. The fits use drmTMB(..., bmdpar=list(bmr=, def=), prior=list(bmd=..., ...)), in which b4 is replaced by the log BMD (coefficient log_bmd), so that the BMD has a prior; efsapriors gives the default priors of EFSA, and bmdefsa does all steps.

prior.weights

prior probabilities of the models, in the order of ...; equal by default.

method

"laplace" (default) for the Laplace approximation of the marginal likelihoods and a normal posterior distribution of the log BMD of each model, or "is" for importance sampling of both (see marglik); importance sampling is recommended when posterior modes are close to the bounds of PERT priors

n, df

number of draws of the final round and degrees of freedom of the proposal of importance sampling (see marglik)

parm

not used; there is one BMD

level

the probability of the credible interval; 0.90 by default, for the BMDL and BMDU

x, object

a bmdbayes object

digits

number of significant digits in the printed output

Value

bmdbayes returns a bmdbayes object, a list with the model-averaged BMD (estimates), the table of the models (models: model, family, log marginal likelihood, prior and posterior probabilities, and with importance sampling the effective sample size), the posterior distribution of the log BMD of each model (posterior: the mean and standard deviation of the normal distribution, or the draws and their weights), the lowest dose above zero, and the arguments. coef returns the BMD, confint the credible interval, and bmdbayesmodels the BMDs and credible intervals of the models, a data frame with the posterior median BMD, BMDL and BMDU of each model.

Details

The posterior probability of model k is proportional to its prior probability times its marginal likelihood p(y | model k). With method="laplace", the posterior distribution of the log BMD of each model is normal with the posterior mode of log_bmd as the mean and its standard error (the curvature of the log posterior) as the standard deviation, so that the median BMD of a model is its posterior mode; the model-averaged posterior distribution of the log BMD is the mixture of these normal distributions with the posterior probabilities of the models as weights. With method="is", the importance sampling draws of each model, weighted by their importance weights and the posterior probability of the model, give both the marginal likelihoods and the mixture, without the normal approximation. The BMD is the median of the mixture, and the BMDL and BMDU the quantiles (1 - level)/2 and (1 + level)/2, the 5% and 95% quantiles of a 90% credible interval.

With random effects, the BMD of the BMD parameterisation is that of the curve of the intercepts, with the random effects at zero (the conditional BMD of bmd).

A model whose marginal likelihood cannot be computed (e.g. the fit did not converge, or its Hessian is not positive definite) gets the weight 0, with a warning. print notes the criteria of EFSA (2022) for a credible interval that is too wide, with the 90% interval: BMD/BMDL above 20, BMDU/BMDL above 50, and a BMDL below a tenth of the lowest dose above zero.

References

EFSA Scientific Committee (2022). Guidance on the use of the benchmark dose approach in risk assessment. EFSA Journal 20(10), 7584.

See also

bmdefsa, efsapriors, marglik, fitpert, priors, bmdma

Examples

pr <- list(bmd = pert(0.1, 1, 5), b2 = normal(8, 1), b3 = normal(-2, 2), sigma = half_normal(1))
fit <- function(model)
  drmTMB(rootl ~ conc, data = ryegrass, model = model,
         start = c(b1 = 0, b5 = 0), fix = c(b1 = TRUE, b5 = TRUE),
         bmdpar = list(bmr = 0.05, def = "relative"), prior = pr)
(ba <- bmdbayes(LL = fit("loglogistic"), W1 = fit("weibull1"), W2 = fit("weibull2")))
#> Bayesian model-averaged benchmark dose, relative deviation 0.05, prior pert(0.1, 1, 5) for the BMD
#> Laplace approximation
#> 
#>          model   family  logML  prior   weight    BMD   BMDL  BMDU
#> LL loglogistic gaussian -27.05 0.3333 0.215716 1.0102 0.7724 1.321
#> W1    weibull1 gaussian -30.57 0.3333 0.006396 0.8108 0.5484 1.199
#> W2    weibull2 gaussian -25.77 0.3333 0.777888 1.3590 1.1538 1.601
#> 
#>                 BMD   BMDL  BMDU
#> model average 1.316 0.8869 1.582
#> 
#> Posterior median and 90% credible interval
coef(ba)
#>      BMD 
#> 1.315526 
confint(ba)
#>           5 %    95 %
#> BMD 0.8869296 1.58189
